scenes.label: A few round brain cells light up yellow together and stay joined by links; below them a slab of wet cement, and a clock ticking.
Two brain cells close up, joined by a thin link; small orange proteins gather on it and the link turns thick and yellow.
An eye, an ear and a heart drop their pieces into three parts of a brain; a yellow seahorse-shaped hippocampus deep inside ties them together.
A brain at night under a moon; yellow beads flow from the hippocampus out to the brain's green outer layer, where coloured patches of memory settle in.

A student asleep in bed under a moon remembers more than a student pulling an all-nighter by a lamp; then four small pictures recap the topic: cells in wet cement, a link made sturdy by proteins, the hippocampus tying pieces together, and sleep replaying it to the cortex.
